hand_checkable.note: One kWp on a 3650 kWh house. It uses 91 percent of its own production and exports 100 kWh a year, so the end of net metering barely touches it and there is nothing to advise. An empty advice is the correct answer here, not a missing one.
hand_checkable.concern: Revised on 2026-08-21, second pass. Key names only: battery_payback_p50_years became battery_payback_mid_years, because these figures are the extremes of a handful of priced combinations and not percentiles of a sampled distribution. This household gets no battery advice, so every one of them is null and nothing about its answer changed.

large_array_small_use.note: Seven kWp on 2200 kWh of demand: the archetypal loser of the 2027 change, exporting 89 percent of what it makes. The curve flattens hard above 5 kWh because the whole house only uses about 6 kWh a day, so a larger battery has nothing to discharge into. Payback 9.2 years at the central cost, which is why the positive rule stands.
large_array_small_use.concern:
Corrected on 2026-08-21. The capacity curve was priced on the household as it arrived, not as it stands after the free routes it was just told to take, and against the contract it was told to leave. The storage gate already read the residual export, so the decision to show a battery at all was honest while every figure behind it was not: the same kilowatt hours were sold once as a free saving and again as a reason to buy storage. Every figure below moved in the same direction, away from the battery. This was the household that carried the price dependent verdict for the whole golden set, at 5.0 kWh and 9.69 years. Corrected it is 3.0 kWh and 12.05 years, three weeks past the twelve year limit, so it is now a no by a hair. No reference household reaches the middle state any more. That is a finding about the product, not about the test: after the double count is removed, storage does not pay back for any of the six.

Revised on 2026-08-21, second pass. No figure below changed value; the names did, and one figure that was recorded here was never asserted by anything. battery_payback_p50_years is now battery_payback_mid_years and battery_break_even_cost_per_kwh is now battery_break_even_mid_cost_per_kwh, because p50 claimed a percentile of a distribution that was never sampled: the payback band is the extremes of nine priced combinations of the installed price and the tariff level, not the tenth, fiftieth and ninetieth percentile of 243 runs the way the headline is. The break even price was recorded here and read by no test at all, so the one figure the Dutch text tells a reader to hold a quote against was pinned by nothing; it is asserted from now on. The payback band itself widened, and that is a change in the answer rather than in a name. It used to move the installed price only, holding the tariffs at their central value, so its optimistic end read as payback at the cheapest quote in the market under tariffs assumed to be exactly right, which is the end that favours buying. The saving now moves with the tariff band as well. The middle is untouched, so no verdict moved: 12.05 years stands, and every reference household is still told a battery does not pay back. The ends recorded below are new, not moved. The break even price gained the two ends of its own band here as well. It is a band in the response now, because it is the annual saving times the twelve year limit and that saving depends on tariffs nobody knows, and the low end is the one the unconditional yes is decided on: a battery is worth it at every combination only if the break even price clears 900 euro per kWh at the tariff level where storage earns least. Recording only the middle would have left that end unpinned.

Revised on 2026-08-26, engine 0.2.0. Not a correction to the advice. The offline production model was centred on solar noon rather than on 12:00, where it had been sitting 38 minutes early, and its daily shape is now scaled by what it sums to rather than by a closed form that ran 0.29 percent high. Every household exports at slightly different hours as a result, so every figure that is priced off an export series moved. No rule, threshold or tolerance moved. This is the household the correction reaches furthest, and it is the one that needs reading rather than accepting. Its verdict changed: BATTERY_DOES_NOT_PAY_BACK became BATTERY_DEPENDS_ON_PRICE, because the middle of its payback band came down from 12.05 years to 11.46 and the limit is twelve. It is back in the state the previous revision recorded it as having left, at 9.69 years, and the sentence in that revision saying no reference household reaches the middle state any more is no longer true. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy: the middle verdict says the answer depends on the quote, which is what a band spanning 6.65 to 17.97 years honestly supports. The break even price moved with it, 672.24 to 706.66 euro per installed kWh. Whether a verdict should turn on the middle of its band alone is still open in docs/decisions.md, and this household is the one that question is about, so it is now a live question rather than a theoretical one.

Revised on 2026-08-29, engine 0.4.0. Not a correction to the advice and not a change to any rule. The PVGIS series was placed twenty minutes late because a row stamped ten past was read as the mean of its clock hour; the anchor is an argument now and the series sits where PVGIS stamped it. This household runs on FallbackProvider, whose day is built over windows centred on the same stamp, so the two very nearly cancel and what is left is the difference between integrating over a window and placing a point inside an interpolation. Break even, the whole band and not only its middle: 601.07 to 600.76 low, 706.66 to 706.29 mid, 812.24 to 811.82 high, all of it 0.05 percent. The verdict, the capacity and the payback band are unchanged, so nothing a visitor is told about this household moved.

marloes_ev_at_night.note: The case that proves the product is neutral. Charging at night gives her 13 kWh of evening and night demand, so the capacity curve keeps rising all the way to the largest battery on offer and the annual saving looks impressive at 743 euro. Fifteen kWh at 675 euro per kWh is 10125 euro, which is 13.6 years, past the warranty, so she is told not to buy it. The free advice above it, charging the car on her own surplus, is worth 536 euro a year and costs nothing. Free routes measured by simulating each intervention on top of the last: shifting the flexible load 145.60 euro, charging the car on surplus 465.57, switching to a dynamic contract 68.69, together 679.85 against a shock of 876.11.
marloes_ev_at_night.concern:
No storage advice at all now, and that is the correction rather than a regression. CONSIDER_BATTERY used to read the export Marloes has as she lives today. The spec and the Dutch copy both say storage is judged on what is left after routes 1 and 2. Charging her car on her own surplus absorbs almost all of it, so the residual falls under the 1500 kWh threshold and there is nothing left for a battery to store. She was previously told to buy one for kilowatt hours the line above had just told her how to use.

sander_heat_pump.note: Somebody home during the day plus a heat pump. Self consumption is already 47 percent so the shifting rule stays silent, correctly: there is little left to move and the presence check blocks it anyway. The heat pump load falls in winter when there is no surplus to store, so the battery saves only 321 euro a year against a 4725 euro invoice and does not pay back.

He was already being told not to buy one, for reasons that were directionally right and numerically wrong.

The anchor repair above reaches this household through its heat pump rather than through its roof: a heat pump reads a temperature series through the same anchor, and the offline table's temperature is a flat monthly value per hour rather than a shape built around the stamp, so it has nothing to cancel against. Its degree hours shift by twenty minutes, consumption 6824 to 6802 kWh, and break even across its whole band, 343.24 to 343.04 low, 403.53 to 403.30 mid, 463.83 to 463.56 high. He is still told a battery does not pay back, by the same margin.
